thread.title: Microsoft: Better Than All Of FAANG - Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)

author: Stefan Redlich
title: Microsoft: Better Than All Of FAANG - Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)
text:
Microsoft ( MSFT ), the third best-performing stock in 2018 in the Dow Jones and one of the best performers of the broad S&P 500, has finally pulled back from its 52-week high and crashed into double-digit territory. It is still up roughly 15% YTD and of the last beacons of stability in these highly volatile markets.
Source: Microsoft Blog
Fundamentally, the company is doing great and the current pullback is a rare opportunity for investors to get a discount on Microsoft. While we cannot tell how low the markets will go, I am convinced that buying high-quality stocks at discounted prices will prove successful in the long run.
What is going on at Microsoft? In retrospect, Satya Nadella showed great timing when he sold out 1/3 of his Microsoft position on August 10, 2018 at an aggregate price of $109.44 whereas the stock currently closed below $100 at $98.23. However, the reasons why Nadella sold had absolutely nothing to do with the reasons that have been dragging down the stock lately, namely a too-hawkish Fed and general angst and anxiety among investors.
Business-wise Microsoft is firing on all cylinders and here are three strong arguments why I view the current pullback as a good opportunity to restart buying shares in Microsoft.
Broad-based growth led by Azure and Gaming As Apple ( AAPL ) shed over a third of its market cap recently, Microsoft has become the most valuable company boasting a market cap of $750B. Its latest quarterly earnings showed very strong revenue growth of 18.6% Y/Y absolutely crushing estimates by $1.22B. Microsoft's three main divisions - Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud and More Personal Computing (really creative name by the way) - all posted double-digit Y/Y growth rates and all three of them are roughly the same size ranging between $8.6B in sales to $10.7B.
The star performer in Microsoft's very profitable product line-up remains Azure within the Intelligent Cloud segment with 76% Y/Y revenue growth. Although that is a rather strong deceleration from the earlier 90% Y/Y growth rates, Azure is still rapidly catching up to Amazon's ( AMZN ) AWS and thus gaining market share in an expanding market.
One product which so far has not been getting the attention I feel it deserves is LinkedIn. In the previous quarter, the platform had 575M members and showing 40% revenue growth and recorded 33% revenue this quarter with record levels of engagement and job postings. Microsoft's investment of $26.2B into LinkedIn is certainly a heavy one but currently that investment is certainly on the right track. Although it is unrealistic that LinkedIn alone will be able to amortize that investment, Microsoft's strategy and vision to make "LinkedIn the essential platform to connect the world's professionals and help them achieve more with experiences powered by LinkedIn and Microsoft graphs" could pay off.
Microsoft's gaming revenues recorded 45% Y/Y growth led by Xbox software and hardware sales, although the latter was positively affected by a low prior year comparable due to timing of Xbox One X launch. Overall MAUs on Xbox Live grew 8% to 57M. As the user base continues to grow towards 100M MAUs so does the opportunity for monetization expand. Microsoft is investing heavily into cutting-edge streaming technology code-named "Project xCloud" which will allow gamers the " freedom to play on the device you want without being locked to a particular device ". This should be seen as another step during the long journey of bringing game streaming towards mass adoption. Microsoft will be able to leverage its massive cloud advantage with Azure and if it succeeds will provide a leading platform for monetizing all that usage. And the gaming market itself is expected to continue to grow at an 11% clip into 2021 . It is a very competitive market with lots of big players from the U.S. and Asia, most notably Tencent, but as Microsoft is not only providing the software but also a lot of the hardware, we can expect the segment continue to grow at double-digit pace.
Resiliency in tumultuous markets Out of the mega-caps in tech, Microsoft has been the most resilient stock during the December carnage, outperforming all of FAANG. Apple dropped 12.5% over the last 20 trading days, Amazon 8.3%, Facebook ( FB ) 5.2%, Netflix ( NFLX ) 4.8% and Google ( GOOG ) 4.3% which is in line with Microsoft's performance of -4.3%.
Even more impressive is that while all of FAANG is at least trading 20% below its 52-week high, Microsoft is "only" off by around 15% but still up 15% YTD. Even mighty Google, the last to crumble from FAANG, has now entered its own bear market being down 23% from its high, while Apple, Amazon, Netflix and Facebook are down as much as 43%.
Compared to the overall markets, Microsoft has also performed much better over the last 20 trading days. Its performance of -4.3% compares to -7.7% from the Dow Jones and -8.7% from the S&P 500 and Nasdaq alike.
Source: Yahoo Finance Historical Prices; visuals compiled with Tableau Desktop
Visually, we can easily decipher that Microsoft has stronger ups and downs than the markets but overall performed much better. Interestingly, while volumes were rather stable during the first 17 days of that 20 day period, they have more than doubled during the last three days in a week where the Dow Jones tumbled 7% amid strongly increasing volume.
Microsoft is not part of that FAANG club but has performed much better and so far successfully avoided most of the scrutiny these stocks have gained:
Apple has tanked amid multiple supplier cuts and iPhone growth concerns fueled by excessive pricing Facebook has been taken to the cleaners as it faces multiple data scandals jeopardizing its business model and raising concerns about the longevity of its platform Amazon's excessive valuation has been rapidly taken down but the stock is still trading at around 70 times earnings Netflix's even more excessive valuation has been cut heavily and rising content costs and negative cash flows have caused investors to flee from the stock. Despite the stock crashing 42%, it is still trading close to a triple-digit PE ratio Google has performed much better than the rest but also couldn't avoid to enter its own bear market. Microsoft, meanwhile, has not produced any scandals and prompted any downgrades, instead it has been remarkably quiet about Big Softie as most of the attention was directed towards Apple and Facebook.
Perennial dividend growth is ahead Microsoft is one of the most solid dividend stocks in the technology sector yielding 1.9% and currently paying an annual dividend of $1.84 per share. That dividend was last raised by 9.5% in September 2018 and continues the company's dividend history of consecutive annual dividend increases since the year 2004.
The current yield is paltry at best but with the growth Microsoft is seeing in its business combined with its 42% payout ratio, its triple-A rating and massive amount of liquidity there is still a lot of dividend growth ahead for Microsoft investors. Surely, I would rather invest at 2%, 2.5% or even a 3% yield but the times when you could snatch Microsoft at a discount are certainly over. It could be that the markets continue to decline and eventually even Microsoft will enter its bear market but it could also be that the Fed reverses its course and the trade war is settled. Getting Microsoft for under $100 is a good starting point for a small position.
If we project 8% dividend growth with a 1.9% starting yield with quarterly dividend reinvestment and 10% annual stock price appreciation we would get the following net dividends (15% tax factored in) for an initial $1,000 investment:
Within 10 years, we would have more than doubled our net YoC and overall stock value. It is a hypothetical example with 8% dividend growth being fairly conservative and 10% annual stock price appreciation demonstrating a slight outperformance to the 8% long-term S&P 500 trend, as I consider Microsoft to be a superior stock compared to the market. Although the mechanics behind reinvesting growing dividends is known to most investors, I still get excited when seeing how this dividend snowball gets bigger and bigger even with a starting yield below 2%.
Investor Take-Away Microsoft is not a bargain but at a forward P/E of 20 and expected double-digit earnings growth rates not expensive either. The company is a leader in Personal Computing and rapidly catching up on the number 1 spot in the cloud markets. It is one of the last beacons of stability in a tumultuous market that is locked in a daily sudden-death mode. Any news regarding interest rates, economy and trade war as well as company-specific news on guidance will nowadays quickly send stocks up or down a few percentage points. That Microsoft has "only" dropped 15% from its high despite the staggering rally it enjoyed earlier is testament to the high quality of the underlying business.
And such a business is rare to get at a decent discount unless a severe recession will hit the economy. Right now I consider the news to be much more negative than the current shape of the economy actually is as despite numerous companies missing guidance, the guidance they are giving is still implying very healthy growth rates just not the lofty expectations of analysts. Apple for instance is guiding to a record holiday quarter of almost $90B in sales but sold off on that guidance and literally crashed the days and weeks after.
In this sudden-death environment, Microsoft could certainly lose another 15% of its value, but if the Federal Reserve gets less hawkish and the trade war is resolved during the first quarter of 2019, it could also easily gain 15. As such, I consider the current valuation to be a sound opportunity for an initial purchase or topping up an existing position but certainly not an all-in buying opportunity either. For long-term dividend investors it is a great stock, although not a screaming buy due to its low starting yield, but with years and decades of perennial dividend growth ahead even the lowest plant can grow into a big tree.
